svg.text: Sites = registrable domains. Web searches, MCP calls and addresses only found in
scripts never count as sites. Flagged = sites with any flag other than failed;
failed is counted on its own. “→ show” turns on the matching quick toggles.
Which sources this session has (FR-13). A missing one reads “Not recorded:

Search, quick toggles, one shared filter
Search covers sites, hosts, commands and search queries. Clicking a site adds
the “Site: …” chip; chips are shared by Topology, Requests and Timeline and kept
Topology · Requests · Timeline, kept in the URL. No pan/zoom canvas and no edge
toggles: the graph is laid out top to bottom by origin and always fits the
Read left to right: where the access came from → which agent and command → which
site. Claude’s web tools, then commands & scripts, then MCP servers; services
and Log Hub are collapsed below.
One node per command or tool. The agent (root, sub-agent, workflow) is a small
label on the node, not a column. A curl started by a script reads “curl, inside
Site name, host when different, requests and ↓/↑ (“?” when not measured). Line
width = requests. Amber = flags, red = failures. ● seen running · ◐ from the
command · ○ found in a script. Size and time are known only for
curl/wget/ssh/scp/sftp and Node.js processes; everything else shows where, not
Found in a script, not seen connecting
api.y.io is written in fetch.mjs, which Claude wrote and ran, but no runtime
source saw a connection: dashed node with ○, not counted as a site.
One node per MCP server with its call count. It ends in a dashed “destination
unknown” box and is never linked to a site. Works the same for any MCP server;
Services Claude started (dev servers) are hidden; Log Hub’s own uploads are
always excluded. Each is one clickable line that opens a drawer with counts —
Clicking a site node or row highlights its path and dims the rest. The panel
says why it is flagged, lists hosts and paths, who reached it and when, and
jumps to Requests, Timeline or the turn.
Site list, synced with the graph
The same sites as rows, grouped by origin, flagged and failed first, then by
requests (every column sortable). Selection is shared with the graph. Big
sessions: top 10 per section, then “+ N more sites ›”.
At most 25 sites are drawn: every flagged or failed site plus the busiest of
each band (partner.io only failed, so it is not counted as flagged). The sites
of one command sit in one block that a single line points to; “+ 125 more sites”
